title: Universal Print: audit records in the Microsoft Purview unified audit log
summary: Hold: the briefing leaves retention and retention-policy coverage unresolved even though Microsoft's unified audit log documentation covers these records. The roadmap facts, audit operations, licensing and control paths are supported.

claims.claim: This roadmap change concerns Universal Print audit logging.
claims.quote: Universal Print: audit logging

claims.claim: Microsoft plans audit records of administrator and user activities including print job submissions, configuration changes and printer registrations.
claims.quote: I can access Universal Print audit records of key administrator and user activities, such as print job submissions, configuration changes, and printer registrations.

claims.claim: The planned records are available in the Microsoft Purview unified audit log for compliance and long-term record-keeping.
claims.quote: Audit records will be available in Microsoft Purview’s Unified Audit Log for compliance and long-term record-keeping.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Cost and licensing: Audit retention
claims.claim: How long audit records remain searchable depends on the licence assigned to the users generating them.
claims.quote: The length of time that an audit record is retained (and searchable in the audit log) depends on your Office 365 or Microsoft 365 Enterprise subscription, and specifically the type of the license that is assigned to specific users.

claims.claim: The standard retention for users on non-E5 Microsoft 365 or Office 365 licences is 180 days.
claims.quote: For users assigned any other (non-E5) Office 365 or Microsoft 365 license, the system retains audit records for 180 days.

claims.claim: Microsoft Entra ID, Exchange and SharePoint activities have one-year default retention for eligible E5 users; Universal Print is not named in that default.
claims.quote: For users assigned an Office 365 E5 or Microsoft 365 E5 license ... the system retains audit records for Microsoft Entra ID, Exchange, and SharePoint activity for one year by default.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Retention policies can retain records in services outside the one-year defaults for up to one year.
claims.quote: Organizations can also create audit log retention policies to retain audit records for activities in other services for up to one year.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Retention beyond 180 days and up to one year requires Office 365 E5, Microsoft 365 E5, Microsoft Purview Suite or E5 eDiscovery and Audit add-on entitlement for the user generating the record.
claims.quote: the user who generates the audit log (by performing an audited activity) must have an Office 365 E5 or Microsoft 365 E5 license or a Microsoft Purview Suite (formerly known as Microsoft 365 E5 Compliance) or E5 eDiscovery and Audit add-on license.

claims.where: Open questions: retention; Risk assessment: Change & support
claims.claim: Whether Universal Print unified audit records receive the 180-day or one-year default remains unpublished.
claims.quote: This default policy retains audit records that contain the value of AzureActiveDirectory, Exchange, OneDrive, and SharePoint for the Workload property ... Audit records for all other activities are retained for 180 days by default
claims.fix: Replace the final Open questions bullet with 'Universal Print unified audit records fall outside the listed one-year workload defaults and are retained for 180 days by default, unless a custom retention policy changes the duration.' Replace 'Universal Print is not named among the one-year defaults, so confirm what applies before promising long-term record-keeping' with that same sentence. Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/audit-log-retention-policies.

claims.where: Open questions: retention; Why it matters
claims.claim: Whether an audit retention policy can cover Universal Print unified audit records remains undocumented.
claims.quote: Record type: The audit record type the policy applies to. If you leave this property blank, the policy applies to all record types.
claims.fix: Remove 'and does a retention policy cover them?' from the final Open questions bullet. The existing Why it matters statement that the unified audit retention regime covers these records is supported: the cited retention page states that a policy with Record type left blank applies to all record types. Do not add a control row.
